raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`get_batch_sizes_to_capture` drops the top decode bucket when `--cuda-graph-max-bs` is below the request pool and not a multiple of the attention-TP alignment. Example: DP attention with attn TP 4 and `--cuda-graph-max-bs 15`. The generated buckets are `[1..8, 10, 12, 14, 15]`, and the pool is 16. The pool endpoint is only appended when the max bucket exceeds the pool. The alignment filter then leaves `[4, 8, 12]`, so batches 13–15 fall back to eager.

The EAGLE draft runners also select buckets as if each request were one row. Each runner's real width is:
- draft decode: `topk`
- draft extend: `num_draft_tokens`
- multi-layer draft extend: the window

At width 1 the alignment filter is stricter than the real row alignment, so those graphs get coarser buckets and pad more than needed.

## Modifications

- `get_batch_sizes_to_capture`:
  - Cap at `min(max bucket, pool)`.
  - Align request counts by `mul_base / gcd(mul_base, width)`. This is the same constraint as `bs * width % mul_base == 0`, applied per request.
  - With padding enabled, always keep the aligned endpoint.
  - With `--disable-cuda-graph-padding`, only configured sizes are captured. This drops the unusable endpoint above the cap.
- `EAGLEDraftCudaGraphRunner`, `EAGLEDraftExtendCudaGraphRunner` and `MultiLayerEagleDraftExtendCudaGraphRunner` pass their `captured_req_width`.
- `EagleDraftWorker` computes the draft-decode and draft-extend bucket lists at their own widths. These lists are used in the capture logs.
- The topk=1 chain constants are sized to the TP alignment (x2 under TBO). This keeps the fast path for the padded top bucket instead of falling back to the slow path (and keeps the megakernel's `[:bs]` slice in range).
- Graph-static buffers size from the padded top bucket. Padding rounds the top decode bucket up to the attention-TP alignment (x2 under TBO), so it can exceed `--cuda-graph-max-bs` (max-bs 15 with attn TP 4 captures 16). New `decode_capture_max_bs` (`cuda_graph_config.py`) and `runtime_context.decode_cuda_graph_max_bs()` are the single bound, used by:
  - the topk=1 chain constants
  - LoRA, inkling sconv, kv-canary
  - dflash/dspark draft samplers and epilogues
  - the CuteDSL MoE token budget
  - the DeepEP v2 and MegaMoE decode dispatch budgets
  - the trtllm native FP4 output buffer
- When no configured bucket is aligned below the pool, keep the aligned endpoint and log it instead of asserting.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A: only CUDA-graph bucket selection and preallocated buffer sizes change; the model forward is unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

None for this branch. This change removes the eager tail for batches above the last aligned bucket when the configured max is unaligned.

## Tests

`test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_decode_cuda_graph_buckets.py` (new) covers:
- pool and max-bs endpoints
- per-phase widths
- TBO
- no-padding mode

It asserts that every batch size up to `min(pool, max_bs)` has a covering bucket.

`test_eagle_worker_v2_topk1_fastpath.py` covers constant capacity under TP and TBO padding.

Bound coverage: the bucket test asserts every captured bucket stays within `decode_capture_max_bs`, plus the accessor (15→16, TBO 17→24, CuteDSL 16×4), kv-canary write capacity (TP 4, max-bs 15 → 16), the MegaMoE padded budget, and the DeepEP v2 `required=128` boundary.

CPU run of the touched suites: `test_decode_cuda_graph_buckets.py`, `test_eagle_worker_v2_topk1_fastpath.py`, `test_cuda_graph_setup.py`, `test_model_runner_decode_rows.py` and `test_oot_eagle_hooks.py`. Result: **39 passed, 12 subtests passed**. With the source change reverted, the unaligned max-bs case (`15-15-1-4`) fails.

Buffer-bound follow-up, CPU, compared against the same suites with the change reverted: bucket, kv-canary, `test_server_args.py`, `unit/spec`, trtllm graph metadata, MegaMoE, CuteDSL AR fusion, kv-canary headroom and the ratchet tests. Result: 8 failures, identical to the baseline (`test_eagle_seeded_coins.py`, `test_fast_prefill_plan.py`). The directly touched files run 367 passed.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).
